speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are suffering from a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to understand the root cause, please tell me how many years you have had these symptoms. Additionally, have you ever smoked, or been exposed to significant environmental dust or chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The combination of an 11-year history of chronic cough with copious, purulent, foamy sputum in a non-smoker is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis rather than simple chronic bronchitis. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of airway damage, I am requesting images of the lungs. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT_scan
